clean_story:
"Even number. Divisible by twelve.
48 is called so because it follows 47 and precedes 49 in the counting sequence. It sits between 36 and 60, two other highly composite numbers, sharing their knack for clean division. Unlike primes, 48 breaks down neatly: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3. This makes it a practical choice for grouping—like splitting a class of 48 students into teams of 4, 6, or 8 without leftovers. In time, 48 hours marks two full days, a span often used for challenges or deadlines. In music, 48 preludes and fugues form Bach’s Well-Tempered Clavier, a cornerstone of classical composition. Its abundance of factors also makes it useful in geometry, where it can tile planes or divide circles evenly. Three related subjects are composite numbers, time measurement and musical structure."
